scope: Proposition 9.1 (The real counting branch) of the manuscript “Cap-selected amplitudes and triangle chords for honeycomb walks” (preprints/Cap-selected-amplitudes-and-triangle-chords-for-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7fd6eb0adc06ad82), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 49. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants N0, C such that, for every N ≥ N0 and |δ| ≤ 1/4, the consecutive equations T(yi) = i − 1 2 + δ, 1 ≤ i ≤ N, have exactly one ordered real solution. Its quantiles belong to BN,s. Throughout BN,s, the Jacobian H in (9.2) is invertible and ∥H−1∥ℓ∞→ℓ∞ ≤ C. For each fixed N, the solution depends locally analytically on δ and admits local analytic continuation under small analytic perturbations of the equations.
